blocks.content: Every person entering upon a constitutional office shall, before taking his seat, make and subscribe an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose.

items: Third Schedule Exception: Oaths of the President, Vice-President, and Governors are NOT listed under the 3rd Schedule.
Oath Cross-Verification: The Chief Justice of India administers the oath to the President, while the President administers the oath to the CJI.
Pleasure Doctrine: The Governor and Attorney General hold office during the pleasure of the President and lack fixed security of tenure.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President takes an oath to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution, administered by the Chief Justice of India.
Oaths for the President (Art. 60), Vice-President (Art. 69), and Governor (Art. 159) are specified in their respective articles, not in the Third Schedule.
The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President, with a customary tenure of 5 years.
Supreme Court judges hold office until 65 years of age, whereas High Court judges hold office until 62 years of age.
The CAG and UPSC members serve for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
